title: run-deck-weekly-operational-snapshot-2027-08-24
content:
SRE Run Deck — weekly operational snapshot (Mon 2027-08-23 -> Sun 2027-08-29)

Owners and attendees
- Note owner: Asha Raman (primary)
- Attendees (weekly sync): Asha R., Daniel P., Maya T., Luis O., Zoe C., plus on-call rotation: Robin S. (night)
- Slack: #sre, #sre-rotations, #ops-bridges

1) Executive summary
- High-level: Stability mostly steady; one notable Sev2 incident (routing fallback regression) on 2027-08-24 that increased end-to-end P50/P95 latency for hosted-api in us-west for ~15 minutes. No data exposure or customer errors beyond 5xx spike; one customer reported increased latency in production.
- SLO impact: small weekly blip — rolling 7d availability fell from 99.95% to 99.92% for hosted-api region-us-west. Still below our quarterly SLA threshold but within tolerance for a single event; follow-ups planned.

2) Incident summary (Sev2) — routing fallback regression (2027-08-24 02:18 UTC)
- Detection: automated latency alert (P95 > 360ms) + user-reported ticket (RED-3189).
- Timeline (local UTC):
  - 02:18 — Latency alert triggered by observability pipeline (traces and p95).
  - 02:20 — On-call (Robin S.) joined bridge; initial hypothesis: increased batching delay.
  - 02:28 — Quick check: batching and queue depths normal; KV cache hit-rate dropped 12% in us-west.
  - 02:34 — Rollout check: a model-routing policy change (canary) had been promoted 02:00 UTC — tied to PR runtime#1945.
  - 02:38 — Mitigation: rollback routing-change to previous variant, restore original prefers-local routing rule.
  - 02:42 — Latency trending back to normal; 02:50 — P95 under alert threshold.
  - 03:10 — Bridge closed after 30m monitoring.
- Root cause (preliminary): subtle mismatch between new routing variant and prefix cache keys that reduced KV cache effectiveness when requests hit variant B; this increased backend fetches and caused higher tail latency under burst.
- MTTR: ~24 minutes from alert to rollback.
- Follow-ups/actions (see section 6).

3) SLO snapshot (rolling 7d, measured 2027-08-17 -> 2027-08-24)
- hosted-api global availability target: 99.95% (rolling) — current: 99.92% (delta: -0.03)
- serving-runtime P99 latency target: 500ms — current weekly: 540ms (driven by the above event; baseline otherwise ~480ms)
- kv-cache availability target: 99.9% — current: 99.87% (cache degradation during event)
- batching throughput target (per-GPU): baseline 1.8k tokens/s — current rolling: 1.75k tokens/s
Notes: The metrics dashboard (per-route) shows the largest deviation in region us-west for the routing rule change window. See linked Grafana panels in the Confluence page.

4) On-call and handoff notes (what incoming on-call should know)
- Current on-call: primary = Robin S.; secondary = Priya K.
- Expected noisy windows: us-west morning traffic spike (13:00-15:00 PDT) this week due to planned model benchmark run by Research. Watch batch queue depth and KV cache hit rates.
- Immediate tasks for next shift:
  - Confirm rollback has corresponding regression tests and add a canary check for cache key stability (owner: Daniel P., JIRA-INFRA-2103).
  - Verify the canary gating rule that promoted runtime#1945 — add an explicit KV cache smoke test to the gating pipeline (owner: Maya T., due 2027-08-27).
  - Re-run synthetic load for us-west with variant B enabled in sandbox and capture cache-hit scatter (owner: Luis O., task created SRE-729).
- Handoff checklist for next on-call: bridge passwords, runbook link, quick triage playbook snippets, and check disk pressure on node labels gpu-x.*

5) Recent operational work and changes this week
- Deployments:
  - runtime#1945 — model-routing gating change (canary promoted then rolled back) — PR link in linked_artifacts.
  - observability#830 — added a P95 anomaly detector for per-region model-routing. Deployed to staging.
- Maintenance windows planned:
  - 2027-08-27 00:00-02:00 UTC — cluster kv-cache compaction (low-risk, but expect transient CPU spike). Ops ticket: JIRA-INFRA-2114.
- Capacity and cost notes:
  - Dedicated pool utilisation steady at 72% (no immediate scale action).
  - We may need to pre-warm burst capacity before next Research benchmark (ticket SRE-741).

6) Action items and owners (short term)
- Add KV-cache smoke test to canary gating pipeline (owner: Maya Thompson, JIRA-INFRA-2103, due 2027-08-27).
- Post-incident deep-dive and RCA writeup for routing-fallback regression (owner: Robin S., JIRA-SRE-729, draft due 2027-08-26).
- Avoid autopromote until new gating is in place (decision: temporary block; owned by Release Eng — Daniel Park to coordinate).
- Create a dashboard alert that correlates routing-variant churn to cache-hit ratio (owner: Zoe Chen, PR: runtime#1951, due 2027-08-30).
- Run sandbox variant B load test and capture traces/kv-keys (owner: Luis Ortega, task SRE-729, due 2027-08-26).

7) Long-lead initiatives and risks
- Model rollout safety: need a small test harness that validates key invariants (cache key preservation, latency under synthetic burst, rollback loop detection). This is a cross-team item — Research + Release + SRE. Proposal being drafted on Confluence.
- Observability debt: our current alerting thresholds do not surface cache-key churn; tracked under JIRA-INFRA-2150. This remains medium priority.
- Regulatory: a customer asked for per-request audit traces for a Private deployment; work required in trace retention policy (security/compliance flagged).

8) Meeting notes & decisions (weekly sync 2027-08-24)
- Decision: Temporarily disable autopromote for model-routing changes until gating smoke test merged. (Action: Daniel P.)
- Decision: SRE will own short-term KV-cache smoke tests; Research will own longer-term invariant tests in their CI.
- Next deep-dive: Routing fallback RCA review scheduled 2027-08-26 10:00 UTC — invite list: SRE, Release Eng, Research.

9) Misc / notes to self (informal)
- Observed odd spike in small-object GC on a subset of cache nodes — possible correlation to compaction job scheduled 8/27. Watcher: Luis O.
- Reminder: document how the routing policy encodes cache key prefixes (poorly documented today) — low-hanging doc win.
- If you get paged outside quiet hours for >3 repeated latency alerts for the same route, escalate to Release Eng lead (we may be looping through variants).

10) Open questions / blockers
- Can Release Eng add an explicit contract test for cache-key preservation on all routing PRs? (Owner: Daniel P. to confirm)
- Is there an existing alert that correlates cache hit-rate delta to model-variant churn? (no — Zoe C. to implement)
- Does QA have a plan to exercise variant B under load before any promotion? (Research/QA to confirm)

Appendix: useful links
- Incident bridge notes: #sre-incident-log (Slack)
- PR (routing): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1945
- RCA ticket (placeholder): JIRA-SRE-729
- Canaries and gating doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/kv-cache-fallback-design

End of run deck.

— Asha
